note: 'Embarrassing' is not a noun meaning of dossier. Core senses are file/folder, dossier, record, and case file.
proposed_english: file; folder; dossier; record; case file

note: Recherche means both search and research; the same spelling also represents finite/imperative forms of rechercher. The current POS says noun only despite listing verb forms.
proposed_english: search; research; searches/looks for; search!/look for! (forms of rechercher, context-dependent)
proposed_pos: noun / finite verb form / imperative form

note: Garde is a noun meaning guard/watch/custody/protection, but the same common form also means 'keeps/guards' and 'keep!/guard!' from garder.
proposed_english: guard; watch; custody; protection; keeps/guards; keep!/guard! (forms of garder)
proposed_pos: noun / finite verb form / imperative form

note: Amoureux does not mean the noun 'love'. It means in love/loving as an adjective and lover/sweetheart as a noun; the surname is irrelevant.
Prévenir very commonly means warn/inform/notify as well as prevent. Teaching only 'prevent' is materially incomplete.
proposed_english: to warn; to inform; to notify; to prevent

note: Est is overwhelmingly also the third-person singular present form of être, 'is'. Limiting the entry to the noun/adjective 'east' would badly misteach one of French's most frequent forms.
Réaliser means carry out/achieve/make and, in modern French, can mean realize/become aware. The current gloss omits achievement and realization senses.
proposed_english: to carry out; to achieve; to make/produce; to realize/become aware; to direct (a film)

note: 'To build' is not a safe general meaning of arranger. Core meanings are arrange, organize, fix, adjust, and in reflexive use work things out/manage.
proposed_english: to arrange; to organize; to fix; to adjust; to suit; to work things out/manage (s'arranger)

note: The current entry omits the basic meaning 'to jump'. Sauter can also skip, explode/blow, sauté, or jump over.
proposed_english: to jump; to skip; to jump over; to explode/blow; to sauté

note: Core meanings 'treat', 'deal with/handle', and 'address a subject' are omitted.
proposed_english: to treat; to deal with/handle; to address/discuss (a subject); to process; to call/label; to treat medically

note: Craindre primarily means fear/dread. The colloquial 'suck/be bad' use occurs especially in ça craint and should be labeled rather than presented as a neutral equivalent.
proposed_english: to fear; to dread; to be bad/suck (ça craint, informal)
